themes.name: blueprint
themes.note: Frontmatter blueprint-* keys are the dark values of the same CSS custom properties (e.g. blueprint-accent is --accent in dark).

display.purpose: The ATS figure on the job page; tabular figures; one per page.

wordmark.purpose: The Fairsheet name beside the sheet mark, rail and phone header only.

body-sm.purpose: Metadata, hints, tags, small buttons, legends, in-panel group headings (ink-2).

control-strong.purpose: Primary and act buttons, active nav, pressed segment at 600.

label.purpose: Uppercase, tracked 0.07em: table headers, title-block and ledger terms, board column statuses. Never an eyebrow above a heading.

extension-body.purpose: Chrome extension popup base size (12px small, 16.5px h2, 21px h1; options page 14/18/24).

shadows.name: floating-layer
shadows.purpose: Only for layers that float over content (the chart tooltip), paired with a 1px rule-strong border.

shadows.name: active-ring
shadows.purpose: A 1px line drawn with box-shadow on the active rail item; a border, not elevation.

motion.name: t
motion.purpose: Duration of every state change (background, border, color).

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Expo-out curve for state changes and the dimension-line draw.

motion.name: draw
motion.value: 520ms var(--ease), scaleX 0 to 1 from the left
motion.purpose: The ATS dimension line draws once, the first time a browser sees a resume's score.

motion.name: turn
motion.purpose: The working mark (amber dashed square) while a tailoring run is in progress.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Rail becomes phone header plus bottom bar; frame drops; tables reflow into entries; 16px gutter.

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: 216px rail, double-rule sheet frame, title block set in the frame corner.

narrative.overview:
Every job is a drawing sheet checked against its specification. The light theme is a cool white drawing sheet ruled in graphite with one ballpoint-blue hand for what the owner does; the dark theme is a blueprint, a Prussian-blue ground with white linework and a pale sodium-yellow hand. Both are the same drawing: one engineered grotesk set like drafting lettering, 1px rules at three weights, square corners, hatching for what was earned and dashed hidden lines for what is absent or still reachable. The fair sheet is the clean copy made from rough work, and the system keeps that promise visually: values are measured, tolerances are drawn, nothing is decorated.

Density is that of an observation table, not a card deck. Pages are ruled tables, ruled strips and flat panels set inside a double-rule sheet frame, with a single framed title block for scan metadata. Depth comes from line weight and two tonal steps, never from shadow; the only lifted object is a floating tooltip. Motion is limited to 180ms state changes and one signature draw: the ATS dimension line extends to its measured length the first time a browser sees a resume's score.

The world refuses the category default of rounded kanban cards with a bright accent and emoji badges, and it equally refuses the neon hacker terminal. Status is told by checking-ink marks that differ in shape as well as hue, so meaning survives without color.
keyCharacteristics: Two complete token sets (drawing sheet, blueprint) with identical roles; dark is its own steps, not an inversion.
One accent per theme, carried by the owner's hand: actions, selection, and what the owner did or can still do.
Three line weights (rule, control, rule-strong) do the work that elevation does elsewhere.
Square containers, 2px controls, and one circle: the drafting balloon.
Drafting lettering (small tracked capitals) for data labels only; tabular figures for every comparable number.
Dashed line means hidden, pending or still reachable, everywhere.

rules.name: The Ballpoint Rule
rules.body: The accent is the owner's hand: actions, selection, focus, and marks for what the owner did or can still do. It never colors a heading, a decorative fill or a checking meaning (good, pending, bad).

rules.name: The Checking Ink Rule
rules.body: Green checked, amber pending, red correction; each has a wash for grounds. A checking ink is always paired with a shape (filled, dashed, ringed, struck) or a word, never hue alone.

rules.name: The Two Sheets Rule
rules.body: Every color token exists in both sets. The dark set is declared twice: under `prefers-color-scheme: dark` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])`, and under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`. A token added to one sheet and not the other is a defect.

rules.name: The Drafting Lettering Rule
rules.body: Small tracked capitals label data: a column, a term, a column status. They never sit above a heading as an eyebrow, and headings themselves stay in sentence case.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number a reader compares (scores, counts, tokens, money, dates in the title block, revision rounds) is set with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. Tables inherit it.

rules.name: The One Title Block Rule
rules.body: A sheet carries at most one framed metadata box, the title block. Every other summary is a ledger or a ruled strip.

rules.name: The Next Action Rule
rules.body: In any row of jobs, the one next action (Tailor now, Resume, Apply) sits at the right edge, right-aligned, on desktop and phone alike.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Panels, cards, buttons, notices and the title block never cast shadows. Only a layer that floats over content (a tooltip, a popover) takes the floating-layer shadow.

rules.name: The Three Line Weights Rule
rules.body: `rule` separates, `control` bounds what can be operated, `rule-strong` frames and heads. Pick the weight by role, never for emphasis.

rules.name: The 2px Ceiling Rule
rules.body: No corner exceeds 2px except the balloon's circle. No pills, no rounded cards.

dos: **Do** use `var(--token)` for every color and define any new token in both the drawing-sheet and blueprint sets.
**Do** bound operable controls with `control` (#7b8187 light) and separate content with `rule`; frame and head with `rule-strong`.
**Do** keep the accent for the owner's hand: primary and next actions, selection, focus, and what the owner did or can still add.
**Do** draw anything hidden, pending or still reachable with a dashed line, and anything earned with the 135deg hatch.
**Do** set every comparable number in tabular figures and every data label in drafting lettering (0.71875rem, 600, uppercase, 0.07em).
**Do** put each job's single next action at the right edge of its row, as an act button (Tailor now), a small Resume button or Apply.
**Do** keep state transitions at 180ms on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` and switch every animation off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** pair every checking ink with a shape, icon or word so status reads without color.
**Do** reflow tables into two-line ruled entries at 860px and below instead of scrolling the page sideways.
donts: **Don't** round containers or give any control more than a 2px corner; the balloon is the only circle.
**Don't** add shadows to panels, cards, buttons or notices; the floating-layer shadow belongs only to layers that float over content.
**Don't** put a panel inside a panel, or frame a second metadata box on a sheet that already has a title block.
**Don't** use the accent to mean good, pending or bad, or to color headings and decorative fills.
**Don't** set `warn-mark` as text or let it carry meaning alone; it is a fill beside a value.
**Don't** place drafting lettering above a heading as an eyebrow or kicker.
**Don't** add page-load choreography; the dimension line's single draw and the working mark's turn are the only animations.
**Don't** introduce a second chart hue without validating it against the chart surface in both themes; `series-1` is the only series.
**Don't** add gradients beyond the two drafting fills (the earned hatch and the rejected mark's strike).
